questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to try and live in the UK and thought an exchange would be a perfect opportunity to do so. Furthermore, I still wanted to be close to home, as well as choose a country where I wouldn't experience a major culture shock.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not have that many expectations for the exchange, but it turned out to be such a great experience that I would recommend to everyone!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult. The information I received was very overwhelming. You receive a lot of emails with a lot of information, and a lot of them are not revelant for anything. If you know who to contact (e.g. your academic advisor from your department), they are very helpful!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was contacted via email about events being held by the uni for exchange students that would ease our arrival to a new country and tell us about University of Bath and what they can offer. Furthermore I was contacted by the Pharmacy Tutor for an induction meeting and contacted by my academic advisor, who was a professor from the Pharmacology Department and who lectured a lot of the lectures from the courses I had chosen. She was a great help in the beginning, as we had a individual meeting, where I could ask questions about the curriculum or the university. She also offered having meetings throughout the semester with other students, talking about our wellbeings or if anything concerned us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. You just have to be aware of deadlines, if you wish to be guaranteed accommodation through the university. The university will notify you though email about this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living in the city, rather than at campus. I had the choice of two city accommodations and chose to live in Aquila Court, which is located 20 minutes by bus from the uni and a 5 minute walk from the city centre. The accommodation was very modern and almost seemed like a hotel. I had my own room and bathroom and shared kitchen with 6 other people, who were all exchange students. Our kitchen was big and so also functioned as a common room for us to hang out. We had to buy everything ourselves; kitchenware, duvets, pillows, bedding etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accommodation was very expensive (39,541.50 kr. for one semester), and also you had to take into account how much money you are going to use on essentials, as the room and kitchen includes nothing!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process was very easy, as the uni sent an email with instructions on how to register

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything you have to do is listed in the email you receive. They use a website called SAMIS where you have to fill in personal information. I didn't have to apply for a visa because of the length of stay in the UK was under 6 months, therefore I only had to send a copy of my flight ticket as proof of the date I entered the UK.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International Mobility before arriving to the UK and academic advisor after arriving to the UK. Both were very helpful and also helpful to know who to ask for help if they didn't know the answer themselves

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had looked at courses available in the course catalogue from last year and prioritised them. A lot of courses had changed since last year, and I found out when I arrived. I didn't get my first priorities, but I still got two courses that I wanted and that was on my list, but just so that you're aware that it can change from year to year

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask and reach out if you have questions or find it difficult! They are very helpful

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had two courses consisting of a total of 15 ECTS

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of courses are very similar to University of Copenhagen. One of the courses had a closed-book exam where you had to use pen and paper instead of a computer, which I found quite difficult as I am not used to a non-digital exam

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is similar. All lectures are recorded, so you can watch them from home. No books are required as curriculum. In workshops you are automatically assigned a group and given scientific articles to read from home, and then you do group work together at campus.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced topics and trends in pharmacology and Advanced drug discovery for biochemists

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I had chosen to take pharmacology courses rather than pharmacy courses, as I didn't have an interest in the pharmacy courses availabe in semester 1, and they all looked very similar to courses I already had on my bachelor's in pharmacy. Pharmacology knowledge is a bit different than pharmacy, but if you want to try something else than what you can have at UCPH, I would definitely recommend trying it out at uni of Bath. 
Advanced topics and trends in pharmacology had a much higer workload and required good memorisation. As an exchange student, I don't think I would recommend this course, as I studied hardcore from morning to evening for two weeks before the exam. Advanced drug discovery for biochemists is a very chill and easy course that I would recommend.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled a bit around the UK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices are mostly the same as in Denmark. Buying food at the supermarket and in cafes is less expensive. Housing was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many socities you can join!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They literally have everything you can imagine

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding a society for the hobbies you like. I really enjoyed the knit and crochet society, who had a knitting café every week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city of Bath and go on trips to surrounding areas in the UK

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy because it's in many ways similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are so friendly and outgoing! I found it difficult in the start to break the "Danish barrier" about it being weird to approach and talk to strangers. But that is definitely the best way to meet new people and make friends, and people are very openminded and won't find it weird at all. I mostly socialised with local students by sitting next to them in class and introducing myself as an exchange student or by interacting with them through socities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the Brits being so friendly, kind and welcoming

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, put yourself out there and have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I will recommend applying for grants. UCPH does not have an Erasmus agreement with the Uni of Bath, while a lot of the friends I made during the exchange got Erasmus grants. So I applied for a lot of other grants. I ended up having my whole exchange being covered by grants in the end, which I am so thankful for!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in a different country and experiencing the bonding experience by making new friends all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritising between free time and studying

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
